mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate indicates tight monetary conditions, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, which negatively impacts S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in >50% of cases when FEDFUNDS is high.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in unemployment rate signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in >50% of cases when UNRATE increases sharply.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) and high interest rates (FEDFUNDS) create a squeeze on consumer and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in >50% of cases when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS rise.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive in >50% of cases during late-cycle when HOUST declines.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) indicates a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative in >50% of cases when PAYEMS grows strongly.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average signals supply chain issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in >50% of cases when INDPRO is below its moving average.

mechanism_narrative: Weakness in both GDP (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates reduced demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in >50% of cases when both GDPC1 and RSAFS are weak.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate during a monetary tightening cycle leads to higher borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in >50% of cases when FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% during tightening.
